stageMeta.title: MCP Client
headerComment: # Stage 13 — MCP Client
# L13 = L12 + the MCP client bridge.  Every plugin from Stage 12 is
# still here — web access, product config, operability, workflow,
# multi-agent, stateful tasks, and the L6 baseline — plus:
#   dsh-mcp-client   MCP client bridge: connects to an external MCP
#                    server (stdio or streamable-http) and registers
#                    its tools on ctx.tools under server-qualified
#                    names (mcp__<serverName>__<rawName>)
# Architecture concept: the Agent's tools no longer come only from
# built-in packages.  The bridge is a CONSUMER of the core ctx.tools
# registry — the same seam dsh-tool-fs and dsh-tool-bash write tool
# schemas into — so an external process's tools become first-class
# model-facing tools with zero changes to the agent loop.  One plugin
# instance bridges one server; mount further instances (unique
# serverName each) for more servers.
# The configured 'demo' server is a placeholder: no MCP server ships
# with this repo, so the spawn fails fast and the stage demonstrates
# the DEGRADATION contract instead.  failOnStartupError: false (the
# default) means activation completes with zero tools from that
# server, the supervisor retries with bounded exponential backoff
# (10 attempts, 500ms doubling to a 30s ceiling) and gives up loudly;
# the agent runs on its built-in tools throughout.  Point command at
# a real server (e.g. npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything)
# and the mcp__demo__* tools appear with no other change.
# The persona is frozen (byte-for-byte identical to L4/L5/L6) so the
# progression remains a single-variable experiment.
stageMeta.driverQuestion: List the tools you can call right now. Are there any whose names start with mcp__demo__? Based on what you observe, explain whether the MCP client reached its configured 'demo' server and what the harness did about the failure.

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client
comments: # MCP client bridge (new in L13): connects to an EXTERNAL MCP server,
# discovers its tools, and registers them on ctx.tools under
# same naming shape Claude Code and Codex use.  inject = [tools],
# satisfied by the core spine.  Its other package imports
# dsh-llm for OPTIONAL image-result admission) are library imports,
# not service injections — no extra plugins are required.
entries.configYaml:
config:
    # One plugin instance = one MCP server; there is no `servers` list.
    # serverName is required ([A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}, unique across live
    # instances) and prefixes every public tool name this server publishes.
    serverName: demo
    transport: stdio
    # Placeholder command: no MCP server ships with this repo, so the
    # spawn fails fast (ENOENT) instead of hanging the boot.  To go live:
    #   command: npx
    #   args: ['-y', '@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything']
    command: demo-mcp-server
    # Degrade vs fail-closed: with the default false, an unreachable server
    # NEVER blocks activation — the plugin comes up with zero tools from
    # this server, the supervisor retries with bounded backoff (defaults:
    # 10 attempts, 500ms doubling to a 30s ceiling, each attempt a warn
    # log) and then gives up with a loud error.  Set true to reject plugin
    # activation when the initial connect or tool discovery fails.
    failOnStartupError: false
    # toolCallTimeoutMs defaults to 60000 — the repo-wide timeout order of
    # magnitude — and needs no override here.
